Package neqsim.process.mechanicaldesign.valve.choke

Class ChokeConditionMonitor

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.mechanicaldesign.valve.choke.ChokeConditionMonitor
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class ChokeConditionMonitor extends Object implements Serializable
Condition monitoring of a choke by comparing the observed flow coefficient with the calibrated theoretical Cv at the actual opening.

Erosion of the trim opens the flow area, so the observed Cv rises above the theoretical curve. Plugging or deposits lower it. A choke that is commanded closed but still passes flow, or whose Cv does not follow an opening change, has a leaking seat or a stuck or disconnected stem. The observed Cv comes from measured flow and pressure drop, see ChokeFlowCoefficient.observedCv(double, double, double); the theoretical Cv comes from a vendor curve or from a characteristic calibrated on a healthy choke.

The same ratio gives the flow capacity of the real choke relative to its design: where the flow of a collapsed choke dimensions the pressure-protection capacity, scale the design collapse flow with ChokeConditionMonitor.Assessment.getCapacityRatio() and keep the deviation inside the accepted limit. The default tolerances are screening values and should be replaced by the acceptance criteria of the asset.

1.0

NeqSim

    • assessSeries

      public ChokeConditionMonitor.Assessment assessSeries(double[] openingPercent, double[] observedCv, double maximumCv, ValveCharacteristic characteristic)
      Assesses a series of operating points against the trim characteristic.

      Points with non-finite values, a negative observed Cv or a theoretical Cv of zero are skipped. The deviation is the median of the point deviations, which is robust against a few transients. If the openings span at least the configured step but the observed Cv moves less than the configured fraction of the theoretical change, the choke is reported as not responding before the deviation is judged.

      Parameters:
      openingPercent - opening at each point [percent]
      observedCv - observed Cv at each point [US Cv]
      maximumCv - Cv at full opening [US Cv], positive
      characteristic - calibrated trim characteristic
      Returns:
      assessment of the series; the deviation and capacity ratio are medians
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the arrays are null or differ in length, maximumCv is not positive or the characteristic is null
